clue.text: Ambitious, like Icarus

definitions.meaning: an ambitious person aims at the top
Icarus of Greek myth flew so near the sun on waxen wings that they melted

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: one figurative (aspiring), one literal (soaring aloft, as Icarus did).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with lofty aims is described by this hyphenated adjective, which literally means soaring at altitude.

clue.text: 23 birdwatchers occupy this

definitions.meaning: the answer at 23 down in its noun sense of an animal's skin or pelt
a camouflaged shelter from which birds are watched

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a pelt (the noun sense of the answer at 23) and a birdwatchers' screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal's skin, and a camouflaged shelter for watching wildlife has the same name.

clue.text: For instance, go with a will

definitions.meaning: Go is a board ..., an instance of the general term
willing or up for it, as in ready to have a try

explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is not the verb but the Japanese board game, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is an example of a board pastime, and being willing to try something is being up for it.

clue.text: Conductor has to take the consequences

definitions.meaning: an orchestral conductor stands looking at the score and players
an idiom meaning accept the unpleasant results of one's actions

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally first: a conductor must turn towards the score.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting blame, and literally describes what a conductor does on the podium.

clue.text: One no good without experience

parts.note: one and you are both impersonal pronouns, as in one never knows

explanation.surface: A person who is useless lacks any practical knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being youthful implies being inexperienced in life.

clue.text: Part of plane, small English one, Welsh have altered

indicators.note: the letters are altered by being rearranged

parts.note: English made small, abbreviated, is E
taken as written

explanation.surface: Welsh people have modified a little English component of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have altered' rearranges E, ONE and WELSH.
explanation.definitionFit: The nosewheel is the landing wheel under the front of an aircraft.

clue.text: It's a fizzy drink

indicators.note: fizzy suggests the letters bubbling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A simple statement that something is a sparkling beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a plain definition of a sparkling wine, but 'fizzy' stirs up the letters ITSA of "It's a".
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, so a drink.

clue.text: Region of England where treacherous shore has trapped wrecked ship, right?

indicators.note: has trapped puts the second part inside the first
a treacherous coastline is dangerously broken up, so the letters are jumbled
wrecked means smashed, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A dangerous coastline has caught a shipwreck somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: SHROE (from 'treacherous' shore) traps PSHI (from 'wrecked' ship) plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border, though it has no coast at all.

clue.text: Cross, bury key part of organ

parts.note: to inter is to bury
B is a musical key
an organ has reed pipes

explanation.surface: An angry instruction to entomb a vital piece of an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the verb meaning to hybridise.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross animals or plants is to mate different strains together.

clue.text: Mistakenly mass-produce only one single protective component of building

indicators.note: done mistakenly, the letters come out in the wrong order
the fodder's two S letters are cut to only one; S is also the abbreviation for single

explanation.surface: A builder errs by mass-producing a lone protective part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only one single' drops one of the two S letters in MASS-PRODUCE, leaving MASPRODUCE, which 'Mistakenly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof course is a waterproof layer laid in a wall to keep rising moisture out of a building.

clue.text: Leader of boys, really awful type

definitions.text: Leader of boys, really awful type

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: The ringleader of a gang of lads is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a badly behaved child, often the one leading the other boys astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilt, unruly child is a classic awful type, and the clue paints such a ringleader.

clue.text: Divided island, one invaded by American ship, shows some trepidation

parts.note: Timor is split between East Timor and Indonesia

indicators.note: invaded by puts the second piece inside the first

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A partitioned island is attacked by a US vessel and fear spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity and apprehension are the same feeling as trepidation.

clue.text: Dreadful prig — he was set aside

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are badly mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A priggish man was shunted aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aside' reads as part of 'set aside' but is the theatrical noun and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside in a play is a remark meant to be heard by the audience but supposedly not by other characters.

clue.text: Embezzler succeeded at first as a gambler

indicators.note: at first places that letter at the start

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
a peculator is one who embezzles

explanation.surface: A fraudster did well initially at betting.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator takes risky financial positions, a gambler on the markets.

clue.text: Joey, who was born just after the war?

definitions.meaning: a joey is a baby kangaroo, and a boomer is an adult male kangaroo

definitions.text: who was born just after the war?
definitions.meaning: people born in the post-1945 birth surge

explanation.walkthrough: A joey is a baby kangaroo and a boomer a male kangaroo, so a joey is literally a boomer's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in the post-war birth surge is so called, and a kangaroo's baby fits literally.

clue.text: When there's no war, no new money goes on something to eat

indicators.note: goes on places the second piece after the first

parts.note: a pea is a small vegetable

indicators.note: no tells us to drop the letter for new from the coin

parts.note: a centime is a small French coin

explanation.surface: In a time without war, fresh cash is spent on food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes the N (new) from CENTIME, a former French coin; 'goes on' puts the remainder after the pea.
explanation.definitionFit: A period free of armed conflict is the time when there is no war.

clue.text: He's moved in — a very short distance, I admit

parts.note: a means one, the Roman numeral I
MM is the abbreviation for millimetre
I grant means I concede

explanation.surface: Someone has relocated only a tiny bit, the speaker concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has come to settle in a new country has moved in.

clue.text: One may be significant to retired lady

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: Something possibly important to a woman who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'significant other' is a partner; the definition leans on that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase significant other names a partner, so the one completing it may be significant.

clue.text: Animal, rather shy, backed up

parts.note: coy means bashful

indicators.note: backed means moved in reverse, so the word up is turned round

explanation.surface: A timid creature that has reversed into position.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Capital PM

definitions.meaning: the Australian city was the seat of federal government from 1901 to 1927
Lord ... was a British Prime Minister under the young Queen Victoria

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a former Australian capital city and a Victorian prime minister of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian city served as interim national capital, and Viscount Melbourne was a British Prime Minister.

clue.text: What girl went through in a book

definitions.text: What girl went through in a book

parts.words: What girl went through in a book
parts.note: Lewis Carroll's Alice passes through a mirror in the sequel to Wonderland

explanation.definitionFit: Through the Looking-Glass is the Carroll book in which Alice steps through a mirror.

clue.text: Sense, and see, smoke rising

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cig is a cigarette

explanation.surface: Use your eyes and note the smoke going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoning, as in there is sense in that.

clue.text: Musical two soldiers put together

indicators.note: two asks for the piece twice

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Two troops assembled for a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical, filmed in 1958.

clue.text: Dropped to floor

definitions.meaning: to knock down or cut down

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a past tense of fall, and a verb meaning to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbled down is the past tense of fall, and to fell a tree or person is to floor it.

clue.text: Only part of photo meant to be seen in book

indicators.note: Only part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Just a portion of a picture was supposed to appear in a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue's end was garbled by OCR; the page prints 'seen in book', so the definition is 'book', not the draft's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, especially a large, heavy one.

clue.text: Girl child interrupted by disputatious person

indicators.note: interrupted by puts the second piece into the middle of the first

parts.note: a mite is a small child
an arguer is someone who disputes

explanation.surface: A youngster is cut off mid-flow by a quarrelsome type.
explanation.definitionFit: Marguerite is a girl's name, a French form of Margaret.

clue.text: Bloody unusual

definitions.meaning: of steak, barely cooked and still red inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a British intensifier but describes underdone meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare steak is barely cooked and bloody, and rare also means uncommon.

clue.text: Puts change in the cash register without moving

parts.note: to stock is to fill up with supplies, here coins
a till is a shop's cash register

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper loads coins into the cash drawer while standing motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'stocks the till', the wordplay is one action; the two pieces are joined as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motionless, frozen in place, is standing absolutely still.
